title: OpenSCAD models (.scad)
summary: A model is evaluated and drawn as one still picture from a named viewpoint.

items.text: 3D primitives: cube, sphere, cylinder (cones too), polyhedron.
2D shapes: square, circle, polygon, and text (flat glyph outlines; extrude or subtract them like any 2D shape).
Transforms: translate, rotate, scale, mirror, multmatrix, resize.
color(): CSS names, #RGB, #RGBA, #RRGGBB, #RRGGBBAA, [r, g, b] and [r, g, b, a]. An alpha below 1 makes the surface translucent.
Booleans: union, difference, intersection, render, intersection_for.
linear_extrude (twist, slices, scale), rotate_extrude, hull of 3D or 2D children, minkowski of convex 3D children.

projection(): the shadow of 3D children on the XY plane (cut = false, the default) or their cross-section at z = 0 (cut = true), as a flat shape that 2D modules and extrusions use like any other. A model that is entirely 2D, for example a projection() drawing sheet, is drawn as a flat top-down view (orthographic) unless a view is chosen; its shapes are flat gray unless colored. For a stronger drawing use --default-color black, or color the shape in the model outside the projection (color("black") projection() ...; colors inside projection() are dropped), and --background to choose the paper (white by default, transparent keeps alpha).

The viewport variables $vpt, $vpr, $vpd, and $vpf hold the camera of the picture, so a model can place geometry relative to it: translate($vpt) rotate($vpr) faces the camera. Assigning them at the top level of the model sets the view; --view, --azimuth, and --elevation win over the model.
Modifiers: ! (show only), * (disable), # (highlight, a translucent copy), % (background, a translucent ghost).
The language: variables, functions, modules with children(), for, if, let, comprehensions, echo, assert, include and use, and the built-in functions.
Curve resolution from $fn, $fa, and $fs.
-D name=value overrides a variable of the model with a number, a boolean, or text.

text() uses the bundled Liberation Sans unless the model names another font; a character the font lacks (such as U+221D) is taken from the bundled Noto fonts, and one that no font covers draws the missing-glyph box and gives one warning.
Modules offset, surface, import, and roof: they are left out and reported.
Functions parent_module, textmetrics, and fontmetrics (they evaluate to undef and are reported), and some argument forms of search().
minkowski of 2D children, of mixed 2D and 3D children, or of non-convex children (a difference, an intersection, a hollow mesh).
hull with a difference or an intersection among its children, or with mixed 2D and 3D children.
multmatrix with a bottom row other than [0, 0, 0, 1].
Animation: one still picture per command; --time only sets $t. Run the command once per view.
-D values that are vectors or other expressions.
The viewpoint: iso (default; a model that is entirely 2D defaults to top), front, back, left, right, top, or bottom.
Replace the azimuth of the view: degrees about the Z axis, 0 from the front.
Replace the elevation of the view: degrees above the XY plane, -90 to 90.
ortho (default) or perspective.
Set a variable of the model; -D is the short form. Repeatable; the later definition wins.
The value of $t (default 0).

The color of surfaces the model does not color (default gray); the alpha is ignored. A flat 2D drawing is gray by default, so --default-color black gives a high-contrast drawing; a color() in the model overrides it.
The most triangles the model may produce (default {{scadMaxTriangles}}).
The picture is 800x800 pixels unless a size option is given; --width, --height, and --scale also size it. The camera fits the picture; nothing is stretched.
The color the picture is flattened over (default white; black, #RRGGBB, or #RRGGBBAA); transparent keeps alpha.
Fail with unsupported-feature instead of leaving a construct out.

Without --strict an unsupported construct is left out and listed in diagnostics[] of the JSON result as {source: scad, severity: unsupported, code: <id>} (without --json, as an 'Unsupported: <id>: <message>' line on standard error). With --strict the first one fails with unsupported-feature and no file is written.
The output of echo() is in echo[] of the JSON result as 'ECHO: <text>' lines; without --json it is written to standard error in the same form.
Also scad-module-surface, scad-module-import, and scad-module-roof: the module and its children are omitted.
A projection needs more work than one projection may do (too many triangles, or a difference or an intersection whose silhouette costs too much to classify): the projection is omitted.
A projection found a mesh that is not a closed solid (its cross-section does not close): the projection is omitted.
A hull has a difference or an intersection among its children.
A hull has both 2D and 3D children.
A minkowski has a child that is not convex.
A minkowski of 2D children.
A minkowski has both 2D and 3D children.
# on a 2D shape that is not extruded: drawn normally, without highlight.
% on a 2D shape that is not extruded: omitted.
multmatrix with a bottom row other than [0, 0, 0, 1]: omitted.
resize over children that contain a difference or an intersection: estimated bounds are used.
An unimplemented built-in function, for example scad-function-textmetrics: the call evaluates to undef.
Severity warning: a questionable argument (an invalid argument, for example) that still renders.
Error code: a syntax error, an evaluation error, or an include that cannot be read; the message names file, line, and column.
Error code: the model needs more triangles than --max-triangles allows.
See the OpenSCAD section of the Scad user guide for the complete list of identifiers.

echo("anchor", "name", [x, y, z]); declares a named point of the model, for a callout or a leader line drawn on the picture later. The echo line is still printed. The point is in the coordinate system where the statement stands: every enclosing translate, rotate, scale, mirror, and multmatrix is applied, so the anchor is a world point. Only the statement form counts; an echo used as an expression, or inside a function, is a plain echo.

A module, for, if, union, difference, intersection, render, color, hull, or minkowski does not move its children, so the point passes through unchanged. An anchor inside resize, linear_extrude, rotate_extrude, projection, or another module that cannot give its children a position is skipped with a scad-anchor-invalid warning.

Severity warning (code scad-warning, the identifier starts the message): a malformed declaration (a name that is not a non-empty string, a point that is not three finite numbers, a named or an extra argument) or an anchor in an unsupported context. The anchor is skipped; the echo line stays.
The same name may be declared more than once; every declaration is kept, in echo order.

With --json, render adds anchors[] for a model: {name, point: [x, y, z], pixel: [x, y], inside}. pixel is the position in the written picture in pixels from its top-left corner (continuous: pixel i spans [i, i+1), so the center of the first pixel is 0.5), projected with the camera that drew the picture, perspective included. inside is true when pixel lies within the picture. Without --json nothing is added.

The pixel steps move the anchors with the picture: --crop, --trim, --resize, --fit, --pad, --flip, and --rotate are applied to pixel, and inside is tested against the final picture. After a --deskew that corrects the image, pixel is null; it is also null for a point behind a perspective camera (inside is then false).
pixel says where a point projects, not whether it can be seen: an anchor hidden behind other geometry still has a pixel and inside true.
This is an independent dialect, not OpenSCAD: pictures and tessellation are not pixel-identical to OpenSCAD and no parity is claimed.
include and use are read only from the model's folder and below, symbolic links are not followed, and a missing include is an error here.

A model can be drawn inside an SVG diagram with <image href="part.scad" .../> (see 'canvasnet help svg'), with the view the library chooses for it (isometric for a 3D model, top-down for a flat 2D model, or the model's own $vp* variables) over a transparent background.
Indexing is lenient: v[i] is undef for a negative or non-finite index, and a fractional index is truncated.

text() is laid out one character at a time without shaping or ligatures; language and script are ignored; size is the height of the glyph H. A generic name (sans, serif, mono, sans-serif, monospace, ...) is a bundled Liberation font; any other family is looked up in the installed fonts (so it can differ between machines), then among the bundled Liberation families, and a family found nowhere is drawn with the bundled Liberation Sans and a warning. For each character the chosen font lacks, the glyph comes from the bundled Noto Sans, Noto Sans Math, or Noto Sans Symbols 2 (never an installed font), with no kerning across fonts; characters nothing covers are listed in one warning per text().
The semantics of the # highlight and the % ghost are this package's documented choices; a ghost is part of the fitted bounds but not of the model.
hull and minkowski constructs they cannot handle are omitted and reported, never approximated; so is a projection that is too complex or whose mesh is not closed.

projection(cut = true) includes a face that lies exactly in the z = 0 plane (a closed section); the silhouette and the section are computed from the tessellated meshes, so a curved solid projects to its polygon.

The viewport variables follow the documented meaning of the OpenSCAD ones ($vpr is the rotation of the camera, so rotate($vpr) turns an object to face it). The model sees the default $vpt = [0, 0, 0], $vpd = 140, and $vpf = 22.5 and the $vpr of the requested view, because the camera is fitted after the model is built; only an assignment of $vpt, $vpd, or $vpf turns off the automatic framing.
The result is a static picture from a named view (iso by default, top for a model that is entirely 2D; orthographic by default), not an interactive camera.
